# Teaching Philosophy

<!-- Replace this section with your own teaching philosophy statement. -->

My approach to teaching philosophy centers on three commitments:
argument, narrative, and collaboration. I believe students learn
philosophical reasoning best when abstract problems are made concrete
through story and interactive engagement.

The use of D&D-style adventure sessions in my courses is not merely
a pedagogical novelty. It reflects a view that philosophy is essentially
a collaborative, high-stakes activity — one where positions must be
defended under pressure, where objections arrive unexpectedly, and
where the quality of your reasoning determines the outcome.

## Courses Documented in This Portfolio

- **PHIL 3XX — Philosophy of Mind** (Fall 2026)
- **PHIL 101B — Introduction to Philosophy** (Spring 2026)
- **PHIL 101B — Introduction to Logic** (Spring 2026)
